{
  "name": "saal_model overview",
  "overview": "The saal_model Airflow DAG runs dbt on Trino to turn Spark-landed Iceberg tables in raw.employee into monthly attendance marts in dataproducts.employee. Right now the reporting month is temporarily hardcoded to July 2026.",
  "plan": "# How the saal_model pipeline works\n\n`saal_model` is an Airflow DAG (`dag_id=saal_model`) defined in [`saal-data-model/flows/saal_model.py`](saal-data-model/flows/saal_model.py). It does **not** ingest Excel or iClock data. Spark DAGs (`employee_data`, leave, onsite) write Iceberg into `raw.employee`; this DAG rebuilds the reporting models in Trino.\n\nSchedule comes from Airflow Variable `AIRFLOW_PIPELINES.saal_model.schedule_interval`, falling back to **manual-only** (`None`). `catchup=False`, `max_active_runs=1`.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  sparkJobs[\"Spark DAGs: employee_data, leave, onsite\"]\n  rawIceberg[\"raw.employee Iceberg\"]\n  airflow[\"Airflow DAG saal_model\"]\n  dbt[\"dbt on worker via dbtRunner\"]\n  trino[\"Trino LDAP\"]\n  staging[\"dataproducts.employee_model views\"]\n  intermediate[\"dataproducts.employee_model tables\"]\n  semantic[\"dataproducts.employee tables\"]\n\n  sparkJobs --\u003e rawIceberg\n  airflow --\u003e dbt\n  dbt --\u003e trino\n  rawIceberg --\u003e trino\n  trino --\u003e staging --\u003e intermediate --\u003e semantic\n```\n\n## DAG graph\n\n```\nstart → TaskGroup saal-data-model-dbt (sequential) → end\n```\n\nFour PythonOperator tasks, in order ([`_DBT_COMMANDS`](saal-data-model/flows/saal_model.py)):\n\n1. **dbt-run-staging** — `dbt run --select path:models/staging/employee`\n2. **dbt-run-intermediate** — `dbt run --select path:models/intermediate`\n3. **dbt-run-semantic** — `dbt run --select path:models/semantic`\n4. **dbt-test** — tests on `employee_attendance`, `employee_attendance_report`, `employee_attendance_status`, `employee_hr_attendance_status`, `employee_departments`, `int_attendance_day`\n\nBecause select is by **path**, history models under the same folders (`*_history.sql`) run with the current and intermediate/semantic layers.\n\n## What each Airflow task actually does\n\n[`run_dbt_on_worker`](saal-data-model/flows/saal_model.py) on the Airflow worker:\n\n1. Load Trino credentials from Airflow Variables (`TRINO_HOST/USER/PASSWORD/PORT/...`) or connection `trino-ldap`.\n2. Use writable scratch `$AIRFLOW_HOME/tmp/saal-data-model-dbt` for logs/target (DAG folder is read-only).\n3. Find dbt in `$AIRFLOW_HOME/dbt_venv/bin` (or PATH / `python -m dbt`).\n4. Strip leftover `dbt_packages` so the run does not need `dbt deps`.\n5. Invoke dbt via embedded `dbtRunner` (`python -c ...`) with `--project-dir` / `--profiles-dir` = package root, `--target prod`.\n6. Pass `--vars` JSON for `attendance_year` / `attendance_month`.\n7. On non-zero exit, raise `AirflowException` with stdout plus tails of `dbt.log`.\n\n[`profiles.yml`](saal-data-model/profiles.yml) profile `saal_data_model` uses dbt-trino LDAP over HTTPS. [`dbt_project.yml`](saal-data-model/dbt_project.yml) sets Iceberg schemas on run start (`dataproducts.employee` and `dataproducts.employee_model`).\n\n## Data flow (dbt layers)\n\n**Sources** ([`models/staging/sources.yml`](saal-data-model/models/staging/sources.yml)): `raw.employee`\n\n- `employee_hr_data`\n- `employee_attendance_metrics` (+ history)\n- `leave_data` (+ history)\n- `onsite_employee` (+ history)\n\n**Staging** (`dataproducts.employee_model`, **views**): clean HR, punches, daily office first/last punch, leave, onsite (ignore onsite `emp_no`; match HR on email).\n\n**Intermediate** (`dataproducts.employee_model`, **tables**, drop-and-recreate):\n\n- `int_hr_roster`, `int_hr_by_prefix`\n- `int_office_day`, `int_onsite_day`, `int_leave_day`\n- `int_attendance_day` — full outer join of office + onsite + leave, then HR overlay (id, emp_code, unique name, truncated email). Grain: `coalesce(business_email, employee_id)` + date. `employee_id` is never an email.\n\n**Semantic** (`dataproducts.employee`, **tables**):\n\n- `employee_attendance_report` — Excel-shaped report for the reporting month\n- `employee_attendance` — copy of that report (replaces old Spark table of the same name)\n- `employee_attendance_status` — punch/leave classification\n- `employee_hr_attendance_status` — weekday roster including missing-punch / unauthorized leave\n- `employee_departments`\n- matching `*_history` incremental snapshots keyed by `reporting_year` / `reporting_month`\n\nReporting window is [`attendance_reporting_bounds()`](saal-data-model/macros/attendance_reporting_bounds.sql): `[period_start, period_end)` for the configured year-month.\n\n## Reporting month (important current state)\n\nIntended order in `_attendance_dbt_vars` (aligned with Spark [`spark_period_env.py`](employee_data/flows/spark_period_env.py)):\n\n1. Env `SAAL_REPORTING_YEAR` / `SAAL_REPORTING_MONTH` (Spark pods get these; this dbt worker usually does not)\n2. Airflow context: **manual** → previous month of `logical_date`; **scheduled** → previous month of `data_interval_end`; timezone **Asia/Dubai**\n3. Else previous calendar month from Dubai wall clock\n\n**Today the function returns immediately with a TEMP hardcode: `attendance_year=2026`, `attendance_month=7`.** The env/context logic below that return is dead until the hardcode is removed. Comment in code: remove after the July run succeeds.\n\nDefault schedule empty means a Trigger DAG run is **manual**, so after the hardcode is gone a trigger on 9 Sep 2026 would use previous month of `logical_date` → **August 2026**, unless env is set.\n\n## How it fits the rest of employee QA\n\nSpark `employee_data` (and leave/onsite) land current-period facts in `raw.employee`. Config notes: run `saal_model` **after** those jobs so `dataproducts.employee.employee_attendance*` refresh from the new punches.\n\nThis DAG is independent (no Airflow TriggerDagRun in the file). Operators run dbt on the worker, not SparkKubernetes.\n\n## Config vs code\n\n[`config/saal_model.json`](saal-data-model/config/saal_model.json) documents the same four dbt commands and Trino `dataproducts.employee`. The live graph is the Python `_DBT_COMMANDS` list, not that JSON, unless another loader still uses the JSON in deployment.\n"
}

`dataproducts.employee.employee_attendance` is **not** loaded from Spark. It is a dbt copy of the monthly report.

[`employee_attendance.sql`](saal-data-model/models/semantic/employee_attendance.sql) is only:

```sql
select * from {{ ref('employee_attendance_report') }}
```

`employee_attendance_report` comes from `int_attendance_day` (office punches + onsite + leave, with HR identity), for the reporting month.

Office punches come from **`raw.employee.employee_attendance_metrics`** (iClock), not from a table named `employee_attendance`.

There is a leftover Spark table `raw.employee.employee_attendance` listed as a dbt source, but **no model reads it**. saal_model overwrites `dataproducts.employee.employee_attendance` with the report so that old name still exists for consumers.

Lineage:

```
employee_attendance_metrics → stg_attendance_event → stg_daily_attendance → int_office_day
onsite_employee             → stg_onsite_employee                         → int_onsite_day
leave_data                  → stg_leave_data                              → int_leave_day
                                                                              ↓
                                                              int_attendance_day
                                                                              ↓
                                                    employee_attendance_report
                                                                              ↓
                                                         employee_attendance
```

Tests currently expect history_period_columns() inside every history file. Selecting * from the existing history report would omit those columns and break tests. The options are updating the tests to allow references to history models, or manually adding the period columns to each file.

The chosen approach is to explicitly list all report columns in the history model while omitting the period fields, then append `history_period_columns()` separately. This avoids duplicating `reporting_year` and `reporting_month` that already exist in the source history table.
